questions.question: Sets are usually denoted by:
questions.explanation: By convention, sets are written with capital letters (A, B, X, Y, …) and their elements with lower-case letters.

questions.question: The symbol ∈ is read as:
questions.explanation: x ∈ A means “x belongs to A” (x is an element of A).

questions.explanation: 14 is even, so 14 ∈ B. 3 and 11 are odd, and 6 is even so 6 ∈ B.

questions.explanation: They have exactly the same elements; order does not matter. So A = B.

questions.explanation: The empty set, with no elements, is written ∅.

questions.question: The difference A − B is the set of elements that:
options: belong to B but not to A
belong to both A and B
belong to A but not to B
belong to neither A nor B
questions.explanation: A − B = { x | x ∈ A and x ∉ B }: elements that belong to A but not to B.

In a class of 40 students, 25 offer Mathematics, 20 offer Physics and 10 offer both. How many students offer neither subject?
questions.explanation: Students offering at least one = 25 + 20 − 10 = 35. Neither = 40 − 35 = 5.

questions.question: The correct relationship between the sets of natural numbers (N), integers (Z), rational numbers (Q) and real numbers (R) is:
questions.explanation: Every natural number is an integer, every integer is rational (n = n/1), and every rational number is real: N ⊂ Z ⊂ Q ⊂ R.
